  • When Borussia Dortmund star Felix Nmecha transferred an imaginary crown from his head onto the pitch last weekend, he probably wasn't expecting to spark a firestorm.
  • Arriving at the German national team camp two days later, he was summoned for a grilling by sporting director Rudi Voller and manager Jurgen Klopp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 20:04 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 05:14 EST, 14 November 2026.

When Borussia Dortmund star Felix Nmecha transferred an imaginary crown from his head onto the pitch last weekend, he probably wasn't expecting to spark a firestorm.

Arriving at the German national team camp two days later, he was summoned for a grilling by sporting director Rudi Voller and manager Jurgen Klopp. His symbol of surrender before God, a goal celebration called ‘The King’s Return’, had blown up into an international news story.

Voller, alongside many of Dortmund’s fans, was concerned by Nmecha's ties to Ballers in God, a network of Christian players founded in 2015 by former Tottenham midfielder John Bostock.

While its core mission is to promote faith in Jesus, the evangelical group is believed to hold a conservative stance on issues such as sexuality and gender – a perspective Nmecha has been in hot water for promoting before.

Nmecha insisted that his message was one of love, but as his celebration was dissected worldwide, the furore posed more questions than it answered. What role does the Christian faith play for footballers? What impact is the groundswell of belief having on dressing rooms? And what should teams do when ancient creeds clash with modern culture?

For months, Daily Mail Sport has been speaking with Christian players, chaplains, and academics. We have found that some footballers are still mocked in dressing rooms for their beliefs. We have also heard tales of elite stars praying with non-League journeymen, and of faith sustaining players through injury crises and rescuing them from dark places after their retirement.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha attracted controversy in Germany for his 'The King's Return' celebration against Elversberg last Saturday.

Manchester City winger Jeremy Doku is one of a growing number of practising Christians in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that for many players, their beliefs and careers are inextricable. Brentford forward Igor Thiago thinks it was part of God's plan for his father to die so that he would become a footballer and share his beliefs internationally.

It has been revealed that 'If my father were alive, I do not think I would have become a footballer, because I think he wanted me to be someone else,' Thiago tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It wasn’t until later that I understood there was a purpose for me to come here and be someone else. To be Thiago, who is a footballer, who can speak about God for so many people, in another language.'.

In a recent development, thiago worked as a fruit-carrier, bricklayer, and rubbish collector from the age of 13 in the streets of Gama, Brazil, to provide for his family after his dad passed away. A career in the Premier League was unimaginable back then. Now he is the main man at Brentford and one of several players at the club professing a Christian faith.

In a recent development, and they are not alone in their devotion. Across the top six divisions, 75 per cent of clubs have a Christian in the first team and almost half regularly host Bible studies or prayer meetings, according to a survey of 134 outfits by Christians in Sport.

In a recent development, their director, Graham Daniels, remembers being told in the 1980s that he was one of just four openly practising Christians in the professional game. An impossible claim to verify, but yes, you read that right, just four. Now you have starting XIs containing more believers than that – and we hear some managers have even been attending church with their squad members. 'There’s a real movement of God within football,' one chaplain at a professional club tells us.

Sources indicate that perhaps God is dwelling in the treatment room, too. Bournemouth winger Ben Gannon-Doak has had three major injuries in his career – to his knee, then quad, then hamstring – and credits his growing faith for helping him recover from each blow.

'With the first, that was before I was strong in my faith – I didn't cope with that one well. I was 17 and felt lost without being on the pitch,' the 21-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport.

Sources indicate that 'The quad injury, I coped better because I started slowly practising my faith more. When my hamstring injury came, I was closer to God than I had ever been before and I coped with that very easily, it was much easier mentally than the other two. I was able to play in the World Cup after that.

Brentford forward Igor Thiago thinks it was part of God's strategy for his father to die so that he would become a footballer and share his beliefs internationally.

Arsenal's 'Bible Brothers' are the most famous band of Christian players – around 10 of their stars including 'pastor' Jurrien Timber (left) pray together before matches.

In a recent development, 'I believe all my injuries happened for a reason and I coped with them the way I did for a reason. I just need to trust God. It makes you stronger, prepares you for things, tests your character. It changes you. Faith has impacted my life in the best way possible.’.

Multiple footballers interviewed for this piece cited the Bible verse Philippians 4:13 – 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' – as a key driver in their life. Gannon-Doak has it tattooed on his left arm.

Football has always had crossover with religion – Manchester City and Everton are among the many clubs to have started as church teams, for example – but the past few years have seen it assume more public prominence.

Arsenal's 'Bible Brothers' are the most famous band of Christian players – around 10 of their stars including 'pastor' Jurrien Timber and Noni Madueke pray together in the hotel before matches, and regularly share Bible verses on social media. Organisations such as F3 and Ballers in God, who hold daily prayers and weekly Bible studies, have built Christian fellowship across the divisions.

According to recent reports, 'Premier League players are on the same call with guys who are semi-pro at step four,' Omar Beckles, a player for League Two Gillingham, tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Lads got together virtually during the pandemic and have been consistently since.' But why the explosion of Christian expression now?

‘An important factor has been the increasing number of players coming from Africa or Latin America, where Pentecostalism and other forms of evangelical Christianity are strong,’ Hugh McLeod, Emeritus Professor of Church History at the University of Birmingham, explains to us.

‘Chaplains interviewed for an academic study in 2011 claimed that elite footballers had “a disproportionate passion for the faith” compared with the average member of society, and they saw the players who had come in from other continents as having a significant influence on this.’.

According to recent reports, an earlier generation of Christian players graduating into management positions, as well as a broader shift in Gen Z asking the cosmic questions in life, has opened up football to the tender matters of faith. Group Bible studies, or even stoppages for Muslim players to break their Ramadan fasts, were unheard of until recent years.

It has been revealed that 'Christians in a changing room can be frowned upon,' indicates Steven Sessegnon, the Fulham academy graduate who now plays for AFC Wimbledon. He was mocked for being baptised.

Marc Guehi was reprimanded by the FA after writing 'Jesus loves you' on Rainbow Laces armbands enforced by the Premier League in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

Daniels, who is now a director at Cambridge United, states Christian values have earned players respect in the dressing room – and thinks faith could alleviate the turmoil players face when the final whistle blows on their career.

‘There was tremendous bullying in the 1980s and 1990s, but the more people saw authentic Christianity, the more they realised that it didn’t harm the changing room, but made it better,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Their integrity shone through – players felt if they talked to Christians, they wouldn’t gossip, and they’d be caring, and they wouldn’t be judgmental.

According to recent reports, ‘In football your identity is achieved. You're as good as your last game. It’s too much pressure for players. That’s why people gamble, drink, and divorce when they retire, because you spent your life having to prove yourself and you don’t know what to do with yourself when you can’t anymore.

'Or think about the academy players who are released at 16. You were the best kid in your class, then your town, your city, your region, the academy system. Then they are released and disappear from the game. Their identity is shot. They feel shame and failure for the rest of their lives.

Recent findings suggest that 'If you know your identity and your purpose is a received gift from God, it’s a complete contrast to everything you’ve ever imbibed. He's going to use your highs and lows in sport to draw you closer to Himself. He’s given you this vocation – this is your gift from Him and He loves you.'.

In a recent development, beckles concurs. ‘Being a Christian actually gives you an unfair advantage in football because you’re always living with some form of optimism and hope,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport.

‘You know there’s no despair. Setbacks are an opportunity to improve and go again. When my dad died, I really saw God show up. He granted me a level of peace and grace and joy just to function at that time when I was grieving.’.

Recent findings suggest that that mentioned, there is clearly an occasional tension between faith and football, which can bring fame, wealth, and temptations untold. Pele, for example, was very open about his low-maintenance relationship with Christianity's bedroom bylaws.

Meanwhile, Daily Mail Sport has heard of stars who have felt compelled to switch church after becoming Premier League regulars as they had become too recognised and overwhelmed by their original congregation.

City star Antoine Semenyo has a close relationship with pastor John Thompson and was baptised on a beach in Bournemouth last December.

Sources indicate that then there's the minefield of political and social issues which footballers are scrutinised over. When playing for Crystal Palace in 2024, Marc Guehi was reprimanded by the FA after writing 'I love Jesus' and 'Jesus loves you' on his Rainbow Laces captain's armband, the wearing of which was enforced by the Premier League in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

Industry observers note that and that brings us back to Nmecha. He could have simply pointed to the sky, or made a sign of the cross, when celebrating against Elversberg last Saturday. It wasn’t his expression of faith, but rather the specific King’s Return action associated with Ballers in God, which riled a certain crowd. No matter that other players, such as Nottingham Forest's Jair Cunha, have deployed the celebration without incident. Klopp states that after their talks, Nmecha will not be repeating it. Dortmund executives will be breathing a sigh of relief.

Sources indicate that the website for The King’s Return campaign initially linked to a live counselling chat run by conservative evangelical organisation Groundwire. There, counsellors espoused the beliefs that homosexuality is sinful and abortion is ‘Satan’s initiative’. When Daily Mail Sport investigated the chat service, we were met with similar views.

It has been revealed that it is not fully clear if Ballers in God agree with Groundwire, or if their members even assume a uniform theological position on such problems, but the network celebrated the scrapping of the Rainbow Laces initiative by the Premier League last year. They appear to have removed the link to the Groundwire chat in the wake of the Nmecha controversy. Daily Mail Sport made repeated requests for an interview with founder Bostock, who has been described as ‘hard to pin down’ and a ‘busy man’, but was turned down.

While high-profile incidents are a PR headache for clubs, there is no need for contrasting moral codes to disrupt a team’s cohesion. ‘You might not agree with someone, but you can respect them and treat them in a non-discriminatory way,’ says Dr Keith Parry, Principal Academic in Sport at Bournemouth University.

‘We’ve had openly gay players and referees at the top level in rugby. It is strange that men’s football is different, but questions around sexuality and inclusion go deeper than religion.

‘There are so many barriers (to players potentially coming out) such as toxic masculinity, fans making homophobic remarks, and so on. There are a lot of Middle Eastern and conservative North American owners in football – how might that impact on inclusion? It depends on the owner.’.

It has been revealed that beckles, who has represented 14 clubs, believes Christian players have a duty to let love rather than division shine through. ‘Footballers are constantly in a world where there’s someone not far from them who will want something from them. Their manager and fans want them to perform, people want their signature, people want them to give them money, their agent wants commercial growth,' he tells us.

Bournemouth and Scotland star Ben Gannon-Doak (right) has the verse 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' tattooed on his left arm.

The young winger credits his faith with helping him through three major injuries.

Industry observers note that 'It’s nice to meet someone that doesn’t want anything from them and genuinely cares for them eternally. That level of love should set people apart.'.

Despite dressing rooms becoming more tolerant of faith, some players still face derision. 'Christians in a changing room can be frowned upon or mocked,' states Steven Sessegnon, a player for League One side AFC Wimbledon, who was taunted after being baptised while at a previous club.

Industry observers note that 'You hear some real nasty things. Some boys don’t understand, which we give them grace for. What scares me the most is why people get so worked up about footballers who are believers.

‘We’re not bothering anyone. We’re going about our business in a loving and caring way. It really rubs people the wrong way and it can cause arguments inside the changing room. One boy was told he will never play because he’s too soft, because he’s a Christian.'.

On matchday, faith is increasingly visible and impacts how players go about their business. The temples are not always glamorous – we hear that some players have even met in the sanctuary of a broom cupboard to squeeze in prayer. Clubs offer what they can. At League One Plymouth, they take the analysis suite – at Arsenal, they have a multi-faith prayer room. Across the pyramid, prayers often ask for protection from injury and the chance to glorify God – but not for a win.

Sources indicate that at Championship Charlton, six to eight players read the scriptures and pray together. 'They have God-given talents and want to use them as an act of worship,' says club chaplain Matt Baker, who is also on hand at the training ground on Fridays to pray with players. 'When you see players do the sign of the cross after scoring a goal, they see it as evangelistic, but it's also expressing to God that I'm doing this for you, for your glory.'.

It has been revealed that at Exeter City in League Two, chaplain George Baker tries to spread the love around the club. 'I'll do the rounds of the stadium and chat to the stewards and grounds staff,' he states. 'It's a great opportunity to value the people who are making matchday happen.’.

Sources indicate that beckles says that religious considerations even factor on the field. 'How do you live with a level of integrity when you want to win? It’s winning in the right way. The “dark arts” are really difficult to navigate,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport, and he is not the only player to express this feeling to us.

'Being a Christian actually gives you an unfair advantage in football because you’re always living with some form of optimism and hope,' notes Omar Beckles (right).

‘In my heart of hearts, I’d like to think I wouldn’t dive to win a penalty – that’s deception. I try my best not to do any of that. But there is the heat of the moment that exposes our nature.’.

Gannon-Doak adds: ‘Players losing their temper, starting fights, that's the stuff I try to avoid. But some of the dark arts, that’s just part of the game.’.

A popular Christian slogan since the 1890s goes as follows: ‘What would Jesus do?’ Typically it is applied to quandaries in a believer’s life – how to treat somebody who has seriously wronged you, for instance.

Industry observers note that not as often has it been wondered: ‘Would Jesus go down if a sweaty centre-back tugged his shirt in the penalty box in the 90th minute?’ But the next time you catch a game, you might just catch an athlete wrestling with that kind of question. What would you do?

With its iconic theme tune, long established time in the weekend TV schedule, and expert analysis, Match of the Day is the most famous football show in the world. Each week the team at the BBC broadcast not one, but two, episodes â bringing viewers all the latest talking points from the Premier League.

Putting on this live broadcast is no easy task, thereâs so many different jobs that get the show to air. BBC Bitesize Careers went behind the scenes on a busy Sunday afternoon to meet just a small number of people involved and to find out more about how they got their jobs on the legendary show.

According to recent reports, cue the music. Do, do, do, dooo, do-do-do-do doooooooâ¦.

Joe Hart on why he loves his job on Match of the Day.

From production management assistants to make up artists, assistant producers to pundits, thereâs plenty of jobs that are involved in putting Match of the Day together each week. Thatâs before mentioning the director, producer, editor, production co-ordinator, vision-mixer, sound-engineer, studio floor-manager, the list goes on. Every role requires a different set of skills and knowledge, with loving football not an essential requirement!

Isabelle Anastasiou on finding your next career step.

With a huge number of roles needed to get a live sports programme on to our screens itâs no surprise that the team at Match of the Day we spoke to all had different routes into the industry.

According to recent reports, some took the apprenticeship route whilst others followed their passion for a subject and went on to study it at university. Meanwhile others worked in areas away from sport, and broadcasting, getting different work experience along the way. Make sure to check out the video above to find out more.

It goes to show that thereâs no one set way of doing things, and everyone has their own career path to follow. One thingâs for sure though, following your passion can be a great place to start.

Of course you might change your mind or start working in a part of the industry you didnât expect to find yourself in, maybe even change jobs along the way. Itâs all part of making your own career path, and youâll be getting skilled up and banking different experiences along the way.

Manchester United have reportedly been alerted to the possibility of re-signing Scott McTominay, with the midfielder considering a return to the Premier League amid uncertainty surrounding his future at Napoli.

The Scotland international has developed into one of the most influential midfielders in Italian football since leaving Old Trafford, and his impressive performances have attracted interest from several European clubs.

According to a TEAMtalk report, negotiations between McTominay and Napoli over a new contract have stalled, and intermediaries are already exploring potential destinations ahead of 2027.

The 29-year-old has approximately 18 months remaining on his current agreement, and the Italian champions are keen to avoid losing an crucial member of their squad.

However, the two parties remain some distance apart in their discussions, potentially opening the door for interested clubs to explore a deal.

Manchester United have been informed about the midfielder’s potential availability, and the possibility of bringing their former academy graduate back to Old Trafford has not been ruled out.

The Red Devils are preparing for a significant squad overhaul under Mauricio Pochettino, with strengthening their midfield expected to feature prominently in their recruitment intends.

Uncertainty surrounding Bruno Fernandes’ future could also increase the need for experienced options in that department.

Chelsea are another Premier League club monitoring developments, with the Stamford Bridge hierarchy appreciating McTominay’s ability to contribute both defensively and offensively.

Meanwhile, AC Milan and Juventus are also keeping tabs on the situation, while several Saudi Pro League clubs are understood to be considering an approach.

McTominay is not actively pushing for an immediate departure and remains open to extending his stay in Naples.

Nevertheless, a return to English football is an attractive possibility, potentially setting up an interesting transfer battle next year.

Were any current Man City players signed during charges period?

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has made more than 250 club appearances since his arrival in 2020.
  • No member of Manchester City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.
  • Those offences all came between 2009 and 2018.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has made more than 250 club appearances since his arrival in 2020.

No member of Manchester City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

Those offences all came between 2009 and 2018. City have denied any wrongdoing and appealed against all of the charges against them.

The club's longest-serving first-team player who was purchased from another club is Portuguese centre-back and club captain Ruben Dias, who joined from Benfica in 2020.

Norway striker Erling Haaland is the next longest-serving arrival, joining from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2022.

Midfielder Phil Foden is the only player to have played for the club during the period in which they breached the league's financial rules, but was not a senior signing having come through the club's youth ranks.

Foden, 26, made his first-team debut in a Champions League match against Feyenoord in November 2017.

Like Foden, versatile midfielder Rico Lewis is also a product of the club's academy but did not make his senior debut until August 2022.

All of the club's other senior players were signed between 2023 and 2026.

สำหรับมือใหม่ที่ยังลังเลว่า แทงบอลออนไลน์ เว็บไหนดี ให้ทำเงินได้ไวและเสี่ยงน้อยที่สุด หัวใจสำคัญคือการเลือกรูปแบบการเดิมพันบนเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ให้เหมาะกับทุนและเทคนิคของตัวเอง เพราะบนเว็บแทงบอลออนไลน์ ยุคนี้ไม่ได้มีแค่การทายผลแพ้ชนะทั่วไป การเข้าใจ 5 รูปแบบยอดฮิตก่อนสมัครแทงบอล จะช่วยให้คุณวางแผนทำกำไรได้แม่นยำยิ่งขึ้น.

การเลือกเว็บแทงบอล ออนไลน์ เว็บไหนดี ที่รองรับระบบ ฝาก-ถอน Auto และ True Money Wallet ควรพิจารณาเว็บตรงที่มีความน่าเชื่อถือ ได้มาตรฐานสากล และปรับอัตราค่าน้ำคงที่.

การคัดเลือกโปรโมชั่นคุ้มค่า ถือเป็นตัวช่วยเพิ่มทุนชั้นดี แต่หากเลือกโดยไม่เช็กเงื่อนไขให้ถี่ถ้วน เครดิตฟรีที่ได้มาอาจกลายเป็นภาระในการถอนเงิน การพิจารณา เว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด จึงต้องดูควบคู่กับความยากง่ายของเงื่อนไขการทำยอดหมุนเวียน (Turnover) ด้วย.

ยอดเดิมพันสะสมรวมทั้งหมด (ได้+เสีย) ที่ระบบกำหนดให้คุณต้องเล่นให้ครบตามเกณฑ์ก่อนถอนเงินออก.

สูตรคำนวณ: (เงินฝาก + โบนัส) x จำนวนเท่าเทิร์น = ยอดเดิมพันสะสมที่ต้องทำ.

สำหรับนักเดิมพันยุคใหม่ที่เน้นความสะดวกและต้องการแทงบอลออนไลน์ ผ่านมือถือ คำถามสำคัญคือจะเลือก แทงบอลเว็บไหนดี ที่หน้าเว็บไม่ค้าง และไม่ต้องเสียเวลาตามหา วิธีแทงบอลในเว็บ หรือค้นหาทางเข้าใหม่ทุกครั้งที่ลิงก์โดนบล็อก การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ที่รองรับแอปพลิเคชันโดยตรง จะช่วยแก้ปัญหานี้ได้อย่างเด็ดขาด.

การวิเคราะห์บอลกับการเลือกเว็บบอร์ดหรือ เว็บแทงบอลออนไลน์ เป็นสองปัจจัยที่ต้องทำงานควบคู่กัน หากวิเคราะห์แม่นยำแต่เลือกเว็บที่ไม่มีประสิทธิภาพหรืออัตราราคาค่าน้ำเสียเปรียบ โอกาสทำกำไรระยะยาวก็จะลดลงอย่างมาก.

การคัดเลือกแทงบอลเว็บไหนดี ในปี 2026 เพื่อให้ได้เว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด เชื่อถือได้ หัวใจสำคัญที่สุดคือการเดิมพันกับเว็บตรงไม่ผ่านเอเย่นต์ การันตีความปลอดภัย 100% การเลือกเว็บพนันบอล ดีที่สุด จะช่วยให้คุณสมัครเว็บบอล และวางเดิมพันได้อย่างมั่นใจ ถอนเงินได้จริงทุกยอดบิล.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Industry observers note that eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

Sources indicate that “You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”.

According to recent reports, this was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and noted “stop”.

Industry observers note that A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM.

The precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury.

Recent findings suggest that so while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed.

The anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

Arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”.

Recent findings suggest that they were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

It was a League Two goal in its simplicity, but that is no criticism. Harrison Neal helped a long ball forward, putting it behind Marli Salmon and Aaron Loupalo-Bi relished the chance to get into a foot race, grappling with the England Under-17 international.

Industry observers note that salmon looked like he had him at one point, but Loupalo-Bi was strong – not to mention composed – and he held off the challenge to slide a left-footed shot through the legs of Illan Meslier, who was making his Arsenal debut. What followed was unique to the magic of an English cup tie.

Recent findings suggest that could the miracle happen? When half-time arrived with Fleetwood still in the lead, you began to wonder. But then you saw Ben White and Martin Odegaard go through intense warm-ups so they could be introduced at the start of the second half and you knew the mountain had become taller.

Tech Report: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1172 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation.
  • Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.
  • Sources indicate that the European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation. These include a move to ease rules controlling the use of pesticides and herbicides, which help fight pests and weeds.

Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.

Sources indicate that the European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default. Safety reviews would only be done in exceptional cases, and regulatory authorities, not the industry, would bear responsibility.

It has been revealed that the commission has said its goal is to cut costs, simplify work for authorities and help farmers stay competitive. Scientists and doctors, however, warn that concerns over human health and environmental impact from these toxic substances are being brushed aside.

The European Commission has said it's responding to complaints from farmers and the agriculture industry to clarify EU rules that govern pesticide use.

A joint statement released in May by 19 food associations, including CropLife Europe, which promotes pesticides, noted complicated administrative procedures and a lengthy approvals process meant farmers were "left without any effective solutions to protect their crops against insects, weeds and diseases," putting food security and livelihoods at risk.

"The existing system of periodic renewal assessment of every active substance has become unsustainable," the commission's press service told DW, citing "chronic delays" and "bottlenecks" in the approval of fresh, more sustainable products.

In recent negotiations, EU member states stated open-ended authorizations should be restricted to "low-risk active substances.".

But their stance is still wanting to extend initial approval periods for other substances to up to 15 years, and a maximum of 25 years for renewals.

It has been revealed that herbert Dorfmann, a center-right Italian member of the European Parliament, said there is currently a yearslong delay in approving new pesticides, including more eco-friendly options, meaning farmers are forced to rely on older substances. Or, if these are banned, go without altogether.

The commission wants to "make the system more efficient and responsive," while guaranteeing that "the protection of human and animal health and the environment remain the highest priorities.".

Dorfmann, who as co-rapporteur is responsible for interinstitutional negotiations on the problem, backs the commission's stance, saying the EU needs "to open up the system for innovation.".

He aims to bring the parliament's proposal on the new pesticide rules to a vote among EU lawmakers before the end of the year.

Ecologists and medical experts, however, have spoken out forcefully against the proposed changes, saying the potential implications for human health and the environment are being downplayed.

In September, more than 500 experts from across the EU signed an open letter calling on the European Parliament to suspend its consideration of the new regulations and conduct an independent investigation into health and environmental impacts.

On October 7, UN rights experts also backed the call for a full review into whether the proposed changes violated the EU's obligations under international human rights law, especially with regard to agricultural workers and children.

Pesticides can persist in the environment, contaminating water and degrading soils. They can also drive biodiversity loss and poison other animals higher up the food chain.

When it comes to humans, the European Environment Agency has stated it was "not yet possible to estimate the burden of disease linked to current levels of exposure to all pesticides.".

However, exposure to chemical pesticides, including banned substances that still persist in the environment, has been linked to various cancers, chronic respiratory disease, neurological disorders and developmental delays, as well as problems with fertility and behavior.

And exposure is widespread: A survey conducted between 2014 and 2021 found that 84% of urine samples from both children and adults in five European countries contained residue from two or more pesticides.

Martina Vijver, scientific director and ecotoxicology expert at Leiden University in the Netherlands, said experts were "deeply concerned" that the EU's current plan "will weaken rather than strengthen the level of protection for pesticide regulation.".

Speaking at the European Parliament in September, she said regular reassessments were key to evaluating the safety of pesticides with new findings, pointing out that the perception of risk changes over time.

"The regulatory system must remain capable of correcting yesterday's decisions with tomorrow's knowledge," she said.

Salome Roynel, a policy officer at the Pesticide Action Network Europe, an NGO based in Brussels, noted the harmful effects of pesticides aren't often fully understood until years later, when the product is up for reconsideration.

"Newly introduced science emerges all the time," she told DW, highlighting how 56 active substances have been banned in the EU since 2011 as a result of periodic reviews.

That includes the insecticide chlorpyrifos, previously used in orchards and on vegetable and cereal crops, which has been tied to harmful effects on children's brain development.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel stated it was "obvious that there was some kind of alignment" between the changes proposed by the EU institutions and the demands of the pesticide lobby.

This echoes a latest report by nonprofit research and campaign group Corporate Europe Observatory, which said Dorfmann and other lawmakers had "copy-pasted […] industry demands" into their regulatory proposals.

Dorfmann denied the lobby influence, telling DW he had met with "both sides, industry and environmental associations," in public debates on the issue.

"The main objective is not to keep old products in the market. The main objective is to bring upcoming ones to the market," Dorfmann noted.

Part of that strategy, he added, would be to help more environmentally friendly "biocontrol" products and low-risk substances to bypass current administrative hurdles and get on the market faster.

It's an idea previously championed by Vijver, who agrees that the current system means more environmentally friendly pesticides are stuck in an administrative "traffic jam." She told DW that biocontrol products could go in a green "bus lane" to ease the way to approval at the European Food Safety Authority, while maintaining crucial safety reviews to filter out the more dangerous products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel also supports the blueprint to speed up approval for biocontrol substances, but noted it needs to be part of a wider system change that includes financial support, monitoring and training to use these newly introduced products, as well as maintaining the restrictions on more harmful chemical pesticides ― not further deregulation.

"If farmers get easier access to synthetic pesticides tomorrow, they would have no incentive to switch to biocontrol," she stated. "It's key to put [biocontrol pesticides] on the market and we fully support that, but… it will not be the silver bullet.".

Manchester United are reportedly considering a move for Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic as Mauricio Pochettino looks to strengthen his attacking options ahead of the January transfer window.

The Croatian international has emerged as an attractive option for the Red Devils, who are keen to improve their goalscoring output after struggling to get consistent performances from their current centre-forwards.

According to a report from The i Paper, Matanovic is among the attacking targets Manchester United’s upcoming manager is considering, with the 23-year-old attracting attention after his impressive performances in Germany.

Pochettino is keen to improve his squad, and the Freiburg forward could offer an interesting solution to his side’s attacking problems.

United have struggled to find a reliable goalscorer this season, with Benjamin Sesko and Joshua Zirkzee failing to establish themselves as consistent attacking threats.

Sesko has also been troubled by fitness problems, increasing the need for another centre-forward who can compete and provide additional options in the final third.

Matanovic has enjoyed an encouraging campaign with Freiburg, registering eight goals and three assists in 16 appearances across all competitions. Standing at 6ft 5in, the Croatian possesses considerable physical strength and could offer something different to United’s existing attacking options.

United will therefore need to carefully consider their options before making a formal approach, but Matanovic could prove an interesting long-term investment for Pochettino.

  • Recent findings suggest that this rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League.

Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.

Recent findings suggest that this rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.

Yellow cards that result in a red card during a match do not count towards a player's tally, as a separate suspension will be served.

The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.

During the opening three rounds of the Champions League, 16 players received two yellow cards, meaning they are now two cautions away from a one-match ban.

Shakhtar Donetsk's Marlon Gomes, Villarreal's Santiago Mourino and Inter Milan's Hakan Calhanoglu are each on three yellow cards, putting them on the brink of a ban.

Players can also be suspended if they pick up six, eight or 10 yellow cards. This would also result in a one-match suspension every time a player hits an even number of yellow cards above four.

Red cards result in a one-match suspension, with Bayern Munich's Michael Olise missing his side's earlier clash with Arsenal after being sent off against Viking in the previous round of fixtures.

Uefa may increase the length of a red card ban for serious offences such as violent conduct.

Marlon Gomes (Shakhtar Donetsk).

Josko Gvardiol (Manchester City).

Matheus Cunha* (Manchester United).

Alessandro Bastoni* (Inter Milan).

Cristian Martinez (Slovan Bratislava).

Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool).

*denotes two yellows that resulted in a red card.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:56 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • It has been revealed that when most footballers are recovering from a serious injury, the stadium is the last place they want to be.
  • According to recent reports, amadou Onana is different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:56 EST, 18 November 2026.

It has been revealed that when most footballers are recovering from a serious injury, the stadium is the last place they want to be. If the team are winning, they feel left out. In difficult times, they feel helpless and frustrated. So the best thing to do is stay away and avoid even watching matches on TV.

According to recent reports, amadou Onana is different. The Aston Villa midfielder has not played since sustaining a serious knee injury during Belgium’s last-16 tie with the United States at last summer’s World Cup and still has some way to go before he can feature again.

Still Onana is playing his part. Dressed in eye-catching clothes, he is often pitchside at Villa Park before and after matches, geeing up the crowd or offering advice and encouragement to younger team-mates. He does the same in the dressing room, where his command of five languages is invaluable. To help new goalkeeper Zion Suzuki settle, Onana is trying to learn basic Japanese.

Villa have missed Onana this season and this week revealed their faith in him by handing the 25-year-old a two-year contract extension through to 2031 on Wednesday – a rare gesture to a man who will not play again for some time.

‘It’s a major one for me,’ says Onana, taking a break from his recovery to speak to Daily Mail Sport in Villa’s giant indoor training facility known as ‘The Barn’.

It has been revealed that ‘When I got injured during the World Cup, (director of football) Damian Vidagany came all the way to Los Angeles to see me. They highlighted massive faith in my ability and who I am as a person.

Aston Villa midfielder Amadou Onana has signed a fresh five-year contract, extending his existing deal by two years and committing his future to the club alongside manager Unai Emery.

It's a show of faith in the Belgian, who has been absent since suffering a serious knee injury at the World Cup.

Industry observers note that ‘Very few players renew their contract while they’re out with such a serious injury, so it’s very gratifying. As for the recovery, it’s going to proposal.

Industry observers note that ‘The start is the hardest bit. Now I’m back on my feet, in the gym and moving weights so I feel like myself again. I’m happy with how it’s going.

‘There is no precise timeline. It’s just a question of seeing how I’m progressing. I’m pretty chilled about it and I know I have to take my time because with such a serious injury, if you come back too early you might re-hurt yourself.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Not many people talk about it but football can be lonely in some aspects. I know we earn a lot of money and do an incredible job, and I’m very grateful for it.

It has been revealed that ‘But there are downsides to it that people have to bring to light. If you go home and it’s total silence – just you and you – it can be very complicated. Throughout my injury, it’s a lonely and dark place at times. Luckily the family and the people around me make a huge difference.’.

In a recent development, onana is an unusual modern footballer. Coaches regularly complain about how few vocal leaders there are among the current generation yet Onana is never afraid to speak up.

He first wore the captain’s armband for Belgium at 21, after Kevin De Bruyne was substituted during a friendly against Germany in March 2023.

Villa need those qualities more than ever. Last summer they lost Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins, who were all important in the dressing room. Even though skipper John McGinn is still around, this is a latest Villa and some of their performances this season have reflected that lack of experience.

A summer exodus of experienced players means Onana's leadership is more crucial than ever at Villa.

Sources indicate that ‘Going to the stadium for the first time wasn’t easy at all,’ Onana admits. ‘Even now when I’m watching games and I can’t help my team-mates, it’s frustrating. But I understand my responsibility at this club as well.

‘I’m not a "young talent" any more. I am part of the leadership group with Belgium and I know what that means. We have plenty of substantial personalities and leaders but whenever they need me, I show up.’.

According to recent reports, communication certainly helps. Onana was born in Dakar, Senegal, and grew up speaking Wolof, the most widely spoken language in that country. He has also mastered French, Dutch, German and English.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Because I’m not in the dressing room all the time, I have an outside perspective on it,’ Onana explains. ‘I am into one-to-one talks, making sure everyone feels OK and comfortable within the team.

‘I can speak to Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, Ibrahim Mbaye and Modou Keba Cisse in French, and I was pleased we signed Leon Goretzka so I can speak to him in German and maintain my level. Japanese is the next one.’.

The messages Villa players really need to heed, though, are the ones Emery delivers.

According to recent reports, players rarely have it easy during their early weeks at Villa. Rogers adapted almost instantly after joining in January 2024 but he is the exception that proves the rule.

‘He made me feel uncomfortable,’ Onana recalls. ‘He took me into areas where I wasn’t ready to go and showed me aspects of my game I needed to be better at.

According to recent reports, ‘He has challenged me over and over again in training and games, and he’s made me a better player, certainly on the ball. He doesn’t care about losing the ball or making a mistake. He wants me to be brave and play.’.

‘He has challenged me over and over again in training and games, and he’s made me a better player,' says Onana of Emery.

The working relationship should continue for some time yet. Emery revealed earlier this month that he had discussed a new contract with Villa co-owner Nassef Sawiris, which would likely make him one of the two highest-paid Premier League managers along with Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta.

The start to this season has been bumpy at times but Onana is convinced Villa are on the right track.

‘Unai Emery is the best manager I’ve had and we are lucky to have him,’ indicates Onana. ‘(Emery's possible new contract) is a massive one for the players, staff and fans.

‘He played a big part in me renewing my contract as well which shows the faith and belief he has in me. What he’s done here, not many managers have done it.

‘We’ve played in Europe four seasons in a row now. We won the Europa League last year. He’s creating a culture that I’ve never seen before. Now we are asking ourselves what else we can achieve. He pushes us to the limit and it seems to work.’.

Onana, you sense, needs to keep himself busy. There is not much peace at home these days: his son recently turned one and keeps his parents on their toes, especially as he has just learned to walk. ‘It’s the best job in the world,’ Onana reflects.

All things being equal, Onana should have at least a decade left as a player but he is already considering the next steps and is studying for his UEFA B coaching licence.

According to recent reports, ‘I think it can make me a better player and give me a better understanding of how coaches see the game,' he says. 'A coach’s job is underestimated. People can’t fathom the time it takes or how much thinking you have to do just to prepare a training session.

‘I’ve been working with 16-to-17-year-olds and it’s a heck of a challenge. It’s pretty interesting trying to work out what coaches are thinking and why they plan certain sessions.’.

Industry observers note that onana's son recently turned one and keeps his parents on their toes. ‘It’s the best job in the world,’ he reflects (Source: Instagram/its_onana).

It has been revealed that emery has long been a master at this and demands total commitment. Many times he has urged his players to think solely about their careers, with other considerations coming later.

Onana could not have reached this level without serious dedication, yet he appreciates that life exists outside football. ‘There were times last season where I would see my wife only twice a week due to all the travelling,’ he reveals.

‘Now I can plan my weeks. Sometimes I can plan a weekend away, be a dad, be a husband. That’s important too. It’s all about balance. Too much of something is never good. I don't think a plumber goes out in the day, works and then comes home and tries to do some plumbing at home.

According to recent reports, ‘If I’m only remembered as a footballer, then I will have failed. Football is my job and I'm very, very dedicated to it, but it's not what defines me. I’m trying to make a positive impact in the world in very different aspects. When I’m gone, that’s what I want people to remember from who Amadou Onana was.’.

Bukayo Saka has once again shown why he is one of English footballâs most admired figures, taking time out to donate over a thousand school uniforms to families struggling with the cost of living crisis.

Hailing from Ealing, Saka gifted the uniforms to four local schools, including Greenford High, where he studied as a youngster.

The Arsenal and England winger visited the school personally to surprise pupils, posing for photos, signing autographs, and helping distribute the uniforms to those in need.

Sharing images of the day on Instagram, Saka wrote: "Special day going back home to launch our school uniform project. Thank you to all the schools, our partners and everybody else who helped us give to the students.".

In 2022, Saka was awarded the Freedom of the Borough of Ealing in recognition of his sporting achievements and his positive influence on young people, following his standout performances at UEFA Euro 2020.

Meanwhile, Outside Greenford High stands a striking mural of Saka, painted in 2021 at the suggestion of a student, celebrating his rise from local schoolboy to football star.

Itâs clear that the community of Ealing loves Saka â and he loves it right back â using his platform to inspire both on and off the pitch.

Effective networking does not come naturally to everyone. Credit: sanjeri/Getty.

Networking is not “random socializing”, says Nessa Carey. It’s a professional skill that can be learnt and developed.

Carey, a UK-based entrepreneur and consultant, explains in a six-minute video why scientists often struggle with networking, drawing on her own experiences while working in industry and academia.

Industry observers note that both Carey and Caroline Dunne, an academic careers coach based in the United Kingdom and Australia, describe how to identify good people to chat to, ask insightful opening questions and circulate effectively in a room packed with strangers. In her six-minute video, Dunne recommends arriving early and says it is fine to leave an event before it formally ends.

The two videos formed part of a session on networking at Nature’s flagship Reframing Precision Medicine conference in London last month.

Also speaking at the conference was Susie Ashfield, a public-speaking coach whose 2025 book Just F**king Say It: The Ultimate Guide to Speaking with Confidence In Any Situation includes a chapter on networking.

Ashfield told attendees that networking does not have to feel uncomfortable or unpleasant. One high-quality connection and follow-up conversation is worth more than 100 business cards, she adds.

Which game will Chelsea's Palmer miss after red card?

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge.
  • Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.
  • According to recent reports, palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.

According to recent reports, palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. That dismissal meant that Palmer was handed a one-match ban.

Recent findings suggest that the England playmaker was shown his first caution for an off-the-ball incident involving Spurs' Mateus Fernandes. He was then shown a second yellow card for a foul on Conor Gallagher.

In a recent development, in most cases, this would be served in that team's next Premier League match. However, Palmer will not miss Chelsea's meeting with United at Stamford Bridge.

Instead, Palmer will be banned for the Blues' EFL Cup fourth-round match away at Liverpool on Wednesday night.

This is because red card suspensions are carried out across domestic competitions rather than being specific to the competition they were received in.

Suspensions for an accumulation of yellow cards across a campaign are served in the competition in which they are received.

So while the Blues will miss Palmer for their trip to Anfield, he will be available to face United three days after the club's cup tie on Merseyside.

Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany.
  • They only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow.
  • In a recent development, the scientists see the work as critical.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany. Keeping the roots intact, conservationists carefully lift shoots from a donor meadow of seagrass and place them in a bag.

They only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow. They've already picked out a prime area for the young plants, which need sandy sediment, shelter from waves and currents and sufficient light and oxygen to thrive.

In a recent development, the scientists see the work as critical. Myriam Spicka, who heads the NGO Seagrass Conservation, says she has "seen the changes" in the more than 30 years she's been diving. And she is not the only one who has witnessed the destruction.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Scientists estimate that around 60% of the Baltic coast's seagrass meadows have disappeared.

It has been revealed that "That's the bad news," stated marine ecologist Thorsten Reusch from the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel . "The good news is that the decline has stopped.".

Underwater seagrass meadows feed and shelter fish, crabs, shellfish and many other species. They improve water quality and slow waves, helping protect shores from erosion. And they store carbon in the seabed about 30 to 50 times faster than forests.

Recent findings suggest that around 70 species of seagrass can be found along the coasts of more than 150 countries. Some grow just below the surface, others at depths of 60 meters or almost 200 feet.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, "Some countries have far more seagrass, particularly in the Indo-Pacific," mentioned Reusch. "There, it can play a major role in their carbon balance.".

But the value of seagrass goes beyond carbon storage. Its meadows in the Baltic are among the sea's most valuable habitats. They shelter wildlife, stabilize the seabed and act as natural filters by trapping particles and nutrients.

Planting individual seagrass shoots is painstaking work so people like Reinhard Helbig are trying to make it easier.

In a recent development, through ZosteraTec, the start-up he co-founded, he helps restore marine habitats, including seagrass meadows damaged by offshore activity, such as wind farm construction. His work begins on the beach.

"Stormy weather helps us. Waves and currents wash seagrass out of the seabed. A day or two later, it washes up here, still fresh," he mentioned.

According to recent reports, the collected shoots are grown and multiplied in ZosteraTec's aquaculture. Several months later, the marine saplings are laid on a plant support. A specially developed machine binds the planted strands with biodegradable thread. The resulting lengths can be laid on the seabed with less diving work.

"We plant here on land to cut down on underwater work. That means fewer dives, and we can do the painstaking work on shore," Helbig said.

Researchers at the Geomar Helmholtz Center in Kiel are also testing new ways to restore seagrass across larger areas, including using seeds.

Marine ecologist Esther Thomsen reaches into an aquarium tank and pulls out a flowerpot containing seagrass.

"Ten percent of the plants in our meadows produce seeds. You can clearly see the seeds sitting inside the seed pod," she noted.

Sources indicate that "The major advantage of restoring meadows from seed is greater genetic diversity. And in the future, we should be able to sow seeds over much larger areas," explained Thomsen.

Reusch from Geomar remarked they currently "think the most promising way to grow meadows that can withstand climate change is to plant individual shoots as a foundation, then sow seeds between them to increase genetic diversity.".

Whether a planting mission is successful is revealed months or even years later.

It has been revealed that thomsen and her colleagues are visiting the first seagrass meadow planted in Germany's Baltic waters in 2021. The divers count shoots, check how densely they grow and record how the meadow has developed.

Recent findings suggest that they then compare it with the donor meadow that supplied the plants. Only that comparison reveals whether the new crop has merely survived or is beginning to function more like a natural one.

According to recent reports, "We've just checked the seagrass meadow, and it's really dense. We counted lots of shoots per square," Thomsen noted. "It's looking really good.".

Secure the king, and the rest will follow.

Behind the scenes, sporting director Andrea Berta lined up the Spaniard’s latest four-year deal, which he signed in October, all the while keeping one eye on the players central to the club's long-term vision.

It has been revealed that most of the deals have been months in the making – talks over Rice’s upcoming contract stretch back to at least March, for example. It also comes after Real Madrid having monitored Rice and Raya for the past year, and Barcelona trying to lure Hincapie away back in June.

This push is central to Arsenal’s desire to forge a dynasty by securing the nucleus of this team for at least the next four years of Arteta's reign, following Gabriel, William Saliba and Bukayo Saka all signing long-term contracts last year.

Arsenal are closing in on upcoming contracts for (L-R) David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber, after also tying down Gabriel and William Saliba last year.

Piero Hincapie (left) is also set to agree latest terms, with the rush of extensions coming after manager Mikel Arteta (right) signed a four-year deal last month.

An agent who has previously dealt with Arsenal revealed why the strategy is beneficial to multiple parties.

Recent findings suggest that he told Daily Mail Sport: ‘They are maintaining the value of their players and ensuring squad continuity, to avoid the possibility of disruption. Now Mikel has got the right blend of players and got rid of the agitators (from earlier in his reign), he wants to keep the group solid.

In a recent development, ‘Too many clubs leave it too late when it comes to contract extensions and sometimes agents are happy to let a contract run down so they can renew from a position of strength. Signing-on fees for both the agent and player, higher wages and commission can be boosted.

‘Though on the flipside, an agent can renegotiate a contract with two more years remaining and say: “If you want us to extend now, we want signing bonuses et cetera”. It also provides further long-term security for your client. It’s smart business all round. Arsenal are champions, the players are happy, why wouldn’t you extend?’.

Rice benefits the most – his pay rise will take him very close to Saka, Arsenal’s top earner, with the winger on a deal worth £350,000 a week.

Now, though, comes the tricky part: who of the remaining first-team squad do they want to commit to? Extending every senior player’s contract in a Premier League world governed by Squad Cost Ratio rules is not particularly feasible. The proposal to make up to 60 job cuts across the club, for instance, is a reminder of the general financial stakes at play.

Sources indicate that the biggest decisions are on the futures of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, both of whom have contracts expiring in 2028. One is the club’s captain, and the other is Arteta’s favourite son.

The injuries and dip in form of the two men last season could be why Arsenal may bide their time. Odegaard managed just 16 league starts with shoulder, knee and muscular problems disrupting his campaign, having also missed a large chunk of the season before with an ankle problem.

According to recent reports, kai Havertz (second left) and club captain Martin Odegaard (second right) are the next big decisions for Arteta. Both are key men but is the time right to capitalise on their sale value?

Havertz's season was even more frustrating, suffering a knee injury on the opening day which required surgery, before subsequent muscular setbacks. He played 90 minutes just once in the title-winning campaign.

Both remain vital to Arteta, but their previous injuries and potentially strong sale value makes committing to improved long-term contracts a more difficult financial decision.

Mikel Merino’s deal expires in 2028, but he is not in the same financial or importance bracket as the above two stars. Ben White’s contract is also up in 2028, but there is an option to trigger a 12-month extension. This group are all in or approaching their peak years: Odegaard and Havertz are 27, White is 29 and Merino is 30.

Given most of the players who have agreed fresh long-term contracts will be past 30 by the time their deals expire, there has to be an awareness of not letting this squad get too old. The average age of Arsenal's starting XI in the Premier League this season is exactly 27 years old. Manchester United (27 years and 86 days) are the only Major Six side whose XIs have been older, while perennial rivals Manchester City are 480 days younger per player.

More broadly, sources say the rush of senior players committing their future to the champions is as much about the healthy culture at the club as it is about the team’s strong chance of scooping up silverware in the seasons ahead.

In a recent development, the environment is a positive one (winning a league title helps, of course) and the players are close with one another. They enjoy going into work, which can’t be stated for stars at every club in the league.

In a recent development, there’s a recognition among players of Arteta’s ability to improve them, both individually and tactically. The Spaniard is a stickler for detail and doesn’t believe in the notion of a ‘finished product’.

It has been revealed that when Rice arrived in July 2023 on the pre-season tour of the US as Arsenal's £105million club-record signing, Arteta described his fresh midfielder as a ‘lighthouse’. Yet last month after the club’s 2-1 victory over Leeds, the manager mentioned: ‘I went to him (Rice) and said, “You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else”.’.

Even Rice is not safe from Arteta's relentless demands for improvement.

The collective trust built between Arteta and his players has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation. And the players want to do that at Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that this season, Rice has been challenged to impact play more in the final third. The collective trust built between Arteta and his squad has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation, rather than a desire. And the players want to achieve that at Arsenal, rather than anywhere else.

Industry observers note that berta deserves a pat on the back, too. Ex-sporting director Edu, a shrewd people person and operator, did a fine job with the cards he was dealt; Saliba, Gabriel and Rice arrived on his watch. Berta has had a very different deck of cards to play with, but has also done well to turn this group into champions.

Sources indicate that much of Arsenal’s nucleus is now secured. But there are tricky decisions still to come for Arteta and Berta.

The ownership of Premier League clubs has never been so crucial. Years ago, football fans probably couldn't care less who owned their club. But now, you must have an owner willing to dip into their deep pockets to fund transfers.

The likes of Newcastle and Manchester City are now essentially being owned by states, while there's an increasing number of billionaires in charge of clubs. If you don't have a rich owner, it's going to be very difficult to be competitive in the greatest league in the world. But which teams presently competing in the Premier League have the richest owners?

Given the fact that football has dramatically changed, and that those who have the most money tend to have the most power, these are how every single Premier League club ranks based on the wealth of their owners.

According to recent reports, brentford fan Mark Benham established his wealth through gambling firms such as Matchbook and Smartodds. He took control of the Bees in 2012 and also owns Danish side FC Midtjylland. He's become a bit of a hero among the fanbase with a statistical model helping Brentford establish themselves as a regular Premier League club, as well as helping build a brand-newly introduced stadium.

Sources indicate that brentford, along with Brighton, are two of the best-run clubs in Europe, never mind just in England. Bringing in young players that can be moulded and grown into stars in the making, and then selling them on to bigger clubs for a huge profit is the way the Bees have operated successfully to become a staple in the Premier League.

In a recent development, in 2022, Acun Ilicali company ACUNMEDYA purchased Hull City. Those in England weren't too familiar with the man, but he's a major deal in his native Turkey. A broadcaster, entrepreneur, international TV producer, businessman and more, the 57-year-old has no shortage of ambition, and this is reflected in his sporting projects.

It has been revealed that he's also had connections to Dutch football team Fortuna Sittard, Irish club Shelbourne, and was briefly on the board of directors at Fenerbahce. His sole focus, however, is now with Hull City, and that bodes well for the newly-promoted club.

Beyond Doug King at Coventry City, there haven't been many better owners in the EFL in recent times. The British businessman became the club’s sole owner in 2023 and has since restructured the club’s financial and operational framework in impressive fashion.

On the pitch, it was a bold call for King to get rid of the long-serving Mark Robins, who was sacked after a fine seven and a half years in charge, and eyebrows were raised when Frank Lampard replaced him. But it turned out to be a stroke of genius, as Coventry clinched promotion to the Premier League after 25 years away. Their net worth could be on the rise in coming years if the Sky Blues manager to cement their position back in the major time.

It has been revealed that tony Bloom made his billions through gambling, specifically poker. He bought his boyhood club, Brighton, in 2009 and has overseen their incredible rise with a clear philosophy and incredible success in the transfer market thanks to a data-driven approach.

Sources indicate that the Seagulls operate by using clever scouting methods to unearth gems from all across the globe to develop before selling them to the highest bidder. The best example of this came when Moises Caicedo was brought in for a nominal fee and became one of the best-performing midfielders in English football. This earned the Ecuadorian defensive midfielder a move to Chelsea for £115 million, making him the most expensive signing in Premier League history.

US billionaire Bill Foley assumed control at the Vitality Stadium in 2023. He's the chairman of Fidelity National Financial, Cannae Holdings and Black Knight Financial Services. He also owns NHL side, Vegas Golden Knights and a stake in French Ligue 1 club FC Lorient.

There was an expectation that the beginning of Foley's time in charge of the Cherries would be in the Championship, but the miracles worked by Gary O'Neil and co in the 2022/23 season ensured the club's top-flight status. There was an influx of signings as a result and the appointment of Andoni Iraola has worked wonders as Bournemouth have pushed towards European qualification - though they must now start a new era with Marco Silva in charge this term.

After several really disappointing years, which saw Sunderland suffer two relegations and languish in League One for a period, the Black Cats have returned to the promised land. In their first season back, they qualified for the Europa League against all odds.

In a recent development, majority owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus is the youngest chairman in football, at just 28 years old, but he also has one of the lowest net worths in the Premier League. Whether they can keep punching above their weight remains to be seen, but it's been an incredible journey up until this point.

Sources indicate that evangelos Marinakis, who also owns Olympiacos, hasn't held back in terms of investing in the transfer market following Nottingham Forest's return to the Premier League. It worked as they managed to stay up during the 2022/23 and 2023/24 campaigns and then flourished in 2024/25, finishing in the top seven and securing European football.

Sources indicate that nottingham Forest have signed an incredible number of players, which is a blessing and a curse as those players helped keep the iconic club in the Premier League. Marinakis is also not shy in making some controversial statements and decisions, one of those being when he hired Mark Clattenburg to become the Premier League's first referee analyst, and the other was boldly sacking Nuno Espirito Santo after he led the team to European football, before appointing four different successors before fianlly settling on Oliver Glasner this summer.

It is yet to be seen if any charges are brought against him and what impact that would have on Tottenham as a result. In the meantime, the north Londoners have been splurging on some huge upcoming signings to avoid a third successive relegation dogfight, with Roberto De Zerbi being handed a war chest that has presented him 39 new signings worth £237 million combined.

Sources indicate that leeds United finished first in the Championship just two seasons and will now be hoping that second season syndrome doesn't kick in. They have plenty of money to avoid the drop. 49ers Enterprises, who also own NFL franchise the San Francisco 49ers, have an accumulative net worth of just over £6 billion.

The West Yorkshire side splashed the cash in the 2025/26 transfer window as they spent £100m on new arrivals, and they are nearing that sum again a year on.

The Friedkin Group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin, completed a majority acquisition of Everton in 2024 which ended years of choppy waters for them under the previous ownership of Farhad Moshiri.

Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harry Maguire and Alexis Mac Allister are among 13 players on the brink of a one-match ban.
  • The first one-match suspensions for yellow card offences in the 2026-27 Premier League season have now been served.
  • Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash became the first players to receive a ban for accumulating five yellow cards before gameweek 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Maguire and Alexis Mac Allister are among 13 players on the brink of a one-match ban.

The first one-match suspensions for yellow card offences in the 2026-27 Premier League season have now been served.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash became the first players to receive a ban for accumulating five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 13 players sitting on four bookings after 10 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

Sources indicate that after that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

Sources indicate that for players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

  • It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.
